match.reason: No existing point teaches autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire leadership styles; the closest ones, the contingency approach and what managers do, are related but cover broader ideas.

draft.title: Leadership style
card: Autocratic
The leader makes decisions alone and expects staff to follow. Communication mostly flows down from the leader.
Democratic
The leader asks staff for their views and involves them in decisions. The leader still has the final say.
Laissez-faire
The leader gives staff a lot of freedom and steps in very little. Staff decide how to do their work.

No style suits every case. Autocratic can suit an emergency or inexperienced staff. Democratic can suit skilled staff, and laissez-faire can suit highly skilled, self-driven staff. Staff may feel more motivated when they have a say.
draft.remember: Match the style to the situation and the staff, because it shapes how motivated staff feel.

a.q: Which leadership style involves asking staff for their views before the leader makes the final decision?
opts: Democratic
Autocratic
Laissez-faire
Directive
a.why: A democratic leader consults staff and involves them, but keeps the final say. An autocratic leader decides alone, and a laissez-faire leader leaves most decisions to staff instead of making a final call.
a.clue: Which style invites staff input but keeps the final say?

b.q: A fire breaks out at Priya's restaurant kitchen, and she tells each worker exactly where to go and what to do without discussion. Which style is Priya using, and why can it suit this case?
opts: Autocratic, because quick decisions are needed
Democratic, because staff views are being sought
Laissez-faire, because staff are trusted to decide
Autocratic, because staff always prefer being told
b.why: Priya makes the decisions alone and gives orders, which is autocratic. Speed matters in an emergency, so this can suit the case. It is wrong to say staff always prefer being told, as the card says only that the style can suit some situations.
b.clue: Who makes the decisions, and does the situation allow time to talk?

b.best: Autocratic, because quick decisions are needed

problems.detail: The distractor 'Autocratic, because staff always prefer being told' uses 'always' where the card says a style 'can' suit a case. Test-wise students can rule it out from the absolute word alone, without knowing the idea.

a.q: Before changing the roster, a manager asks the team what works for them, then makes the final call. Which style is this?
opts: Democratic, because staff give input but the leader decides
Autocratic, because the leader makes the final decision
Laissez-faire, because staff are given a say in the roster
Laissez-faire, because the leader steps back from deciding
a.why: The manager consults staff and still keeps the final say, which is democratic. It is not autocratic, because an autocratic leader decides alone without asking staff first.
a.clue: Does the manager ask first, and who decides in the end?
